# Two Magnitude Estimates for the 1906 Earthquake

Two approaches have produced different magnitude estimates for the 1906 earthquake: 7.7 and 7.9. The estimates come from different ways of measuring the earthquake’s size.

A seismic analysis estimated a magnitude of 7.7, using usable recordings from 12 of the 96 observatories studied. A USGS re-evaluation of geodetic measurements estimated 7.9, based on changes in angles and distances between benchmarks.

The estimates reflect different measurement methods—seismic recordings and ground deformation. Different methods can produce different estimates of earthquake size.
